content: Indapamide, commonly referred to as a water pill, is prescribed to alleviate swelling and fluid retention associated with heart disease. It is also used to manage high blood pressure. This medication works by prompting the kidneys to eliminate excess water and salt from the body through urine. In some cases, indapamide may be prescribed for other medical conditions. If you have questions about its use, consult your doctor or pharmacist for further information. Indapamide is available in tablet form and is typically taken orally once a day, usually in the morning. It is important to follow the instructions on your prescription label carefully. If you have any doubts or need clarification, ask your doctor or pharmacist. Take indapamide exactly as directed. Do not take more or less of it, or take it more frequently than prescribed. While indapamide helps control high blood pressure, it does not cure the condition. Continue taking the medication even if you feel well, and do not stop taking it without consulting your doctor. Indapamide is also used to treat swelling and fluid retention caused by medical conditions other than heart disease. Discuss the potential risks of using this medication for your specific condition with your doctor. Before taking indapamide, inform your doctor and pharmacist if you are allergic to indapamide, sulfa drugs, or any other medications. Additionally, provide a list of all prescription and non-prescription medications, vitamins, and supplements you are taking, especially corticosteroids, digoxin, indomethacin, lithium, probenecid, and any other relevant drugs. Notify your doctor if you have a history of heart rhythm problems, diabetes, gout, or kidney, liver, thyroid, or parathyroid disease. If you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding, inform your doctor. Do not breastfeed while taking this medication. If you become pregnant while on indapamide, contact your doctor immediately. If you are scheduled for surgery, including dental procedures, inform your healthcare provider that you are taking indapamide. Be aware that this medication may cause drowsiness. Avoid driving or operating machinery until you know how it affects you. Alcohol can exacerbate the drowsiness caused by this drug, so exercise caution. Follow your doctor’s dietary instructions while taking indapamide. They may recommend increasing your intake of potassium-rich foods, such as bananas, prunes, raisins, and orange juice, depending on your condition. If you miss a dose of indapamide, take it as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and continue with your regular schedule. Do not take a double dose to compensate for a missed one. Frequent urination may occur for up to six hours after taking a dose of indapamide, but this side effect typically decreases after a few weeks of use. If you experience severe or persistent symptoms such as muscle cramps, drowsiness, dizziness, confusion, thirst, upset stomach, vomiting, stomach cramps, decreased sexual ability, or blurred vision, inform your doctor. If you experience serious side effects, such as rapid and excessive weight loss, severe skin rash with itching, or difficulty breathing or swallowing, contact your doctor immediately. Serious side effects should also be reported to the FDA’s MedWatch Adverse Event Reporting program online or by phone. Store indapamide in its original container, tightly closed, and out of reach of children. Keep it at room temperature, away from excessive heat and moisture (do not store it in the bathroom). Dispose of outdated or unneeded medication properly, and consult your pharmacist for guidance on disposal. In case of an overdose, contact your local poison control center at 1-800-222-1222. If the individual has collapsed or is not breathing, call emergency services at 911. Keep all appointments with your doctor and laboratory for regular monitoring of your blood pressure and occasional blood tests. Do not share your medication with others. If you have questions about refilling your prescription, consult your pharmacist.
